page: Microsoft Azure E16-8s_v3 is an ESv3-family virtual machine configured with 8 vCPUs and 128.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU allocation is fully dedicated, backed by a cache hierarchy consisting of a 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB L3 cache. The hardware configuration includes a 262 GB local SSD and supports Premium Storage, while containing no GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear trade-off between compute power and memory capacity. The server exhibits weak to poor CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core results in the bottom 10% and multi-core results in the bottom 25%. Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores fall into the bottom 25% category. However, memory bandwidth benchmarks for both cached small blocks and uncached large blocks perform at an average level. Passmark CPU, memory, and database operations also achieve average tier rankings, whereas static web serving and Redis SET operations remain weak.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB of RAM per vCPU, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense CPU processing. The dedicated CPU allocation and Hyper-V virtualization provide a stable environment, though the weak single-core performance limits its suitability for compute-heavy tasks or large-scale LLM inference. It is best suited for memory-intensive applications, database caching, software compilation, and moderate database operations where RAM capacity is the primary bottleneck.
